intro: Arizona runs its elections county by county, through each county recorder and county elections office, under the Secretary of State.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state, county, and local offices, plus any measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Early ballots go out by mail on Oct. 7 to voters on the Active Early Voting List and to voters who asked for one. You can also vote early in person at your county elections office or any early voting site in your county. Oct. 30 is the last day to vote early in person.

dates.label: Last suggested day to mail your ballot back
dates.detail: After this date, drop your ballot at a drop box, an early voting site, your county elections office, or any voting location in your county on Election Day.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Voting locations are open 6 am to 7 pm. If you are in line by 7 pm, you can vote. Mail ballots must be received by 7 pm.

id_rule.text: Bring ID to vote in person, on Election Day or early. Show one photo ID with your name and address, such as an Arizona driver's license or ID card, a tribal ID, or a U.S., state, or local government ID. Or show two items with your name and address, such as a utility bill or bank statement from the last 90 days, your vehicle registration, or your voter registration card. If you can't show ID, you can vote a provisional ballot and show ID to the county recorder afterward.
